video_title: Airbnb Is Building a ‘Company Brain’ for AI Agents
gist: Airbnb CTO Ahmed Aldal describes Project Everest, a 'company brain' capturing institutional knowledge for agents, and warns that naive markdown memory causes context poisoning, favoring progressive disclosure. He details Airbnb's multi-model, eval-driven approach (cost-vs-accuracy Pareto, small post-trained models for high-TPS search), nuanced token governance anchored on roadmap compression, and AI resolving ~50% of support chats while two-sided dispute mediation remains a frontier problem.

insights.claim: Airbnb is building Project Everest, a 'company brain' that collects institutional knowledge from employees' AI workflows into a shared context pool of how people do things that isn't in the documentation.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Institutional-knowledge capture for agents is an emerging enterprise AI layer beyond code-repo access.
insights.quote: we have something that we call you know project Everest which is effectively kind of like the company brain

insights.claim: Everest started with product engineers but is spreading to product marketers (Airbnb's PMs) and eventually design, aiming at a company-wide context graph built from everyone's workflows.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Context graphs are moving from engineering tools to cross-functional enterprise infrastructure.

insights.claim: Extracting and encoding institutional knowledge so agents can learn from it is, in the CTO's view, an underexplored area compared with connecting agents to codebases.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Whitespace for vendors building enterprise memory / knowledge-capture for agents.
insights.quote: This is like underexplored but something that we've been working on.

insights.claim: Everest is evaluated with consistent benchmark tasks, e.g. having a non-expert engineer land a pricing-rule-change PR in Airbnb's pricing domain (one of its most complex), measuring whether it is faster and more accurate with Everest context.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Enterprise memory systems need task-level evals to prove value and avoid drift.

insights.claim: Airbnb is not convinced it has the right architecture for Everest yet; it is experimenting between a database and markdown files with a harness deciding directory structure.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Enterprise agent memory architecture remains unsettled — no dominant design yet.
insights.quote: I'm not convicted that we have the right uh architecture for it yet.

insights.claim: Markdown files work well for agent memory because frontier models have been trained to navigate file systems.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: File-system-native context is a cheap, effective default for agent knowledge bases.
insights.quote: markdown files are really good because Frontier models have been trained to navigate file systems

insights.claim: The CTO doubts vector search will scale to a company-wide knowledge system.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward pure vector-DB retrieval for enterprise agent memory; favors hybrid approaches.
insights.quote: I find it hard to believe like a vector search is going to scale to to where we need it to work.

insights.claim: Naively accumulated markdown memory causes context poisoning: models are very good at finding old or wrong extracted knowledge.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Memory curation/staleness management is a key unsolved problem and product opportunity.
insights.quote: the the model's like very good at finding the thing that's old >> or wrong

insights.claim: Airbnb expects to land on a hybrid with an intelligence layer doing progressive disclosure of context, because revealing too much context too quickly is the biggest mistake.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Context routing/progressive disclosure middleware is a likely architectural winner.
insights.quote: the biggest mistake you can make is you reveal too much context too quickly to the model

insights.claim: A key open risk is whether Everest stays useful or becomes corrupted as it scales, and whether it will need a rewrite.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Shared agent memory may degrade at scale; watch for governance tooling.
insights.quote: Are we going to corrupt it as we scale it? We don't know,

insights.claim: Agent productivity requires 'MCP-ing' the entire company and documenting complex domains (e.g. regulated payments) in-repo so agent-generated PRs are reviewable by domain teams.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Platform readiness (MCP coverage, in-repo docs) gates AI coding ROI.
insights.quote: how do you basically like MCP your entire company so that an agent can sort of access what it needs

insights.claim: Airbnb balances AI velocity with 'craft': beyond PR throughput and token rates it tracks defect ratios and reliability metrics as guardrails.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Quality metrics alongside throughput mitigate AI-generated tech debt.

insights.claim: Airbnb deliberately avoided token leaderboards, token-maxing and draconian token limits, instead analyzing the shape of adoption: zero-usage users need support, heavy users get investigated.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Contrast with firms that over-spent on agentic coding; nuanced spend governance.
insights.quote: we didn't have token leader like we didn't really focus on token leaderboards

insights.claim: Investigating heavy token users revealed two cases: some needed help building efficiency into workflows, while others were running valuable large migrations that justified the spend.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: High token spend is not inherently waste; migrations are a high-ROI use.

insights.claim: Outliers like pinning a max-thinking frontier model on every subagent with ~10,000 tool calls are flagged as slow and often unnecessary.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Model routing to cheaper/faster models is a growing cost-control lever.

insights.claim: Sam Charrington cited Uber as an example of a company that encouraged unlimited agentic coding and then found it very expensive.
insights.speaker: Sam Charrington (host)
insights.so_what: AI coding cost overruns are a real enterprise budget risk.

insights.claim: Airbnb anchors on downstream metrics: PR throughput shows more output but not more useful output, so the best indicator of good AI use is the roadmap shifting right and compressing.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Roadmap compression, not token usage, is the KPI to watch for AI ROI claims.
insights.quote: the best indicator that you're using AI well is your road map is shifting to the right and compressing

insights.claim: The CTO concedes there is no perfect metric linking AI use to business impact, but argues trend lines matter more than confounding factors if you ship more faster.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: AI ROI measurement remains fuzzy industry-wide.
insights.quote: there is no perfect metric >> on whether your AI use is resulting in business impact

insights.claim: AI has collapsed the sequential artifact cascade (MLE, engineer, designer, PM, legal, policy) because everyone, including designers, PMs, legal and policy, can now jump straight to a code prototype.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Org structure and workflow change may matter more than raw token usage for productivity.
insights.quote: Everyone's just like writing code including the designers, including the PMs, including policy, including legal

insights.claim: Airbnb is a multi-model shop: internal tool Air Chat wraps other harnesses with Airbnb's MCPs and lets engineers choose agentic tools, since being single-vendor is 'crazy' given industry pace.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Enterprises avoid lock-in to a single AI coding vendor; harness/model choice is commoditizing.
insights.quote: given the pace of the industry it's a little crazy to be an X shop

insights.claim: Airbnb runs agentic evals of Airbnb engineering tasks, built with a council of senior engineers, across open and closed-source models, scored by a calibrated LLM judge and plotted as cost versus accuracy.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Internal cost/accuracy Pareto charts drive model procurement decisions.

insights.claim: When models cluster around 92-93% judge scores, it signals either weak evals or that models are good enough, making selection a cost, efficiency and speed trade-off.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Model commoditization pressure on frontier pricing for many enterprise tasks.

insights.claim: The CTO is suspicious of evals that fail to separate frontier from non-frontier models, questioning task difficulty and judge calibration.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Eval saturation can mislead buyers into either over- or under-paying.
insights.quote: I'm very suspicious the eval if we're not able to get some separation between frontier and non-frontier

insights.claim: His hot take is that models are already good enough for many consumer experiences; frontier progress targets the jagged edge of hard enterprise problems rather than reliable consumer tasks.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Consumer AI value may accrue to app owners with small specialized models rather than frontier labs.
insights.quote: my hot take was like the models are good enough for a lot of consumer experiences

insights.claim: Given tight latency requirements and scale, Airbnb post-trains smaller open models with its own RL environments to beat frontier models on narrow benchmarks like policy-adherent customer support.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Demand for open-weight models and post-training/RL infra rises among large consumer platforms.

insights.claim: Airbnb search uses the smallest possible model, post-trained, specialized and distilled, because its TPS is so high.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: High-throughput consumer workloads favor small distilled models over frontier APIs.
insights.quote: we take like the smallest model possible because our TPS is so high

insights.claim: Nvidia's Nemotron was named as one of the good small models Airbnb evaluates, alongside a broad stable of models.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Nvidia gains mindshare in enterprise open-weight small models.

insights.claim: Airbnb built customer-support agent frameworks before open-source alternatives existed but will rebase onto open source if it gets ahead, and contributes back.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Build-vs-buy in agent frameworks is fluid; open-source can displace in-house stacks.

themes.theme: AI customer support in a two-sided marketplace

insights.claim: Airbnb's AI agents already resolve about 50% of all customer support chats/tickets end-to-end without human assistance.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Material support-cost leverage at Airbnb's scale.
insights.quote: we resolve about uh 50% of all um chats with with AI

insights.claim: Airbnb treats support AI as a quality improvement rather than pure cost-cutting, discloses that users are talking to an AI, offers action cards, and escalates to a human on request.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Transparent, escape-hatch support design protects trust/NPS while automating.

insights.claim: Tens of percents of users refuse to talk to AI and want a human even for simple informational queries, a psychological rather than capability barrier.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Caps near-term automation ceilings regardless of model progress.
insights.quote: those are going to be the hardest ones to resolve for because it is really it's like a it's psychological

insights.claim: Two-sided marketplace dispute mediation is a frontier AI problem: adversarial parties, unverifiable evidence (e.g. AI-edited photos of damage), and the need to apply policy neutrally.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Full support automation for marketplaces is far off; human ops remain necessary.
insights.quote: I can easily take a picture of a table, work with AI to like modify the table and say well I came to this place and look at the table. It's missing a leg.

insights.claim: Current models cannot do a great job mediating multi-party disputes; Airbnb keeps human judgment on the hardest cases while doing R&D.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Multi-agent/multi-party mediation is an open research and product opportunity.
insights.quote: the models today can't really do a great job um of like mediating between me and you

insights.claim: Offline agents run at scale behind the scenes to detect payment disputes, fraud and quality issues or bad on-trip experiences, reinforcing trust in the marketplace.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Back-office AI improves trust and safety without UX risk.

themes.theme: Agentic search, MCP access & trust moat

insights.claim: Airbnb is testing a natural-language search box (where, with whom, why) that still returns multimodal results and keeps users in control rather than having AI pick a single property.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Incremental AI search rather than chatbot-first UX for travel booking.

insights.claim: Users don't want a chat box for booking; tests show long text back-and-forth is friction.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Chat-first commerce UIs may underperform structured search in travel.

insights.claim: Travel booking takes weeks, is social/multiplayer, and involves repeated browsing and wishlisting before spending e.g. $10,000, so AI should enhance exploration rather than remove agency.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Agentic one-shot booking may be a poor fit for high-consideration travel.

insights.claim: Asked about exposing Airbnb as an MCP server for third-party agents (an argument eroding due to computer use, per the host), the CTO said decisions will be case-by-case based on best user experience.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Airbnb is guarded on opening inventory to external agents; disintermediation risk managed.

insights.claim: In travel 'convenience isn't key, trust is'; Airbnb's moat is insurance, a trusted payments stack and customer support versus a random MCP server booking a $10,000 trip.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Trust infrastructure is Airbnb's defense against AI-agent disintermediation.
insights.quote: convenience isn't key trust is

insights.claim: Roughly 40% of US humans use AI for travel inspiration, per the CTO's rough estimate, but inspiration also comes from Instagram, videos, friends and events.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: AI is a major but not exclusive top-of-funnel for travel.

insights.claim: Airbnb's roadmap aims to move from a core stays marketplace to 'everything you can do in the physical world' on its platform while reinventing its tech stack to be AI native, with unannounced launches coming.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Signals platform expansion beyond stays; watch for new product launches.
insights.quote: everything that you can do in the physical world is now on our platform

insights.claim: Because Airbnb's roadmap is deeper than its headcount, AI is used to pull in and compress the roadmap rather than expand it; companies without such backlogs should ask if they are ambitious enough.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: AI productivity gains translate into faster execution of existing plans at Airbnb.

insights.claim: CEO Brian (Chesky, transcribed 'Brian down') has a local 'second brain' context graph trained on every document, vision doc, manifesto and email he has received or written, which he uses to reason through his day.
insights.speaker: Ahmed Aldal (Airbnb CTO)
insights.so_what: Top-down AI adoption signal; executive-level personal context graphs.
